beats.direction: Use the recurring witness with an on-screen disclaimer: CITY CONTEXT / NOT DAY-SPECIFIC.
beats.voice: Copenhagen turns participation into an evidence problem: admission, time, teardown, rights, screening, product data and institutional memory each demand a record. This chapter follows backstage coordination: The same field that helps a show run—a name, measurement, image, availability or location—can also make labor newly trackable and extractable.
beats.onScreen: Then: The current framework uses submitted survey responses and documentation, reviewed by an external committee led by Rambøll.
beats.credit: Scandinavian Academy of Fashion Design · CC BY-SA 4.0

beats.direction: Animate only line reveals and state changes in the original evidence diagram.
beats.voice: The current framework uses submitted survey responses and documentation, reviewed by an external committee led by Rambøll. That earlier record fixes a point in time; it does not prove an inevitable progression toward the present.
beats.onScreen: Now: CPHFW and Renoon announced an AI-supported screening pilot for AW27 after a year of testing; human-led screening is stated to continue.
beats.credit: Graphic © Rayven-Nikkita Collins; sources in claim ledger

beats.direction: Animate only line reveals and state changes in the original evidence diagram.
beats.voice: The distinction is material. A polished interface can survive after its workers, contracts, specifications or permission trail disappear, leaving the audience with an outcome but not its operating history.
beats.onScreen: Next: Public materials do not yet provide the pilot model card, training data, error rates, appeal path, energy measurement or independent bias evaluation.
beats.credit: Graphic © Rayven-Nikkita Collins; sources in claim ledger
